AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **0 (Not the asshole)** **Here's why, clearly and compassionately:** ### ️ **You are absolutely justified in standing firm on your court-ordered time.** - **The court order is legally binding** — it exists to protect *both* parents' rights and the child's stability. Your ex cannot unilaterally override it " for the son's sake" or " because he's having fun." If she wants to reschedule, **she must agree with you** (not dictate terms). - **Her pattern is manipulative:** - " *It's for your son* " is a common tactic to guilt-tr you into giving up your time. - Last week: She asked to keep him Wednesday " for the cousin," then rescheduled Thursday last-minute to a lake trip. - This week: She's taking him to an amusement park * during your scheduled time* and expects you to " give up more time tomorrow" for her family party. **This is not about your son — it's about her convenience.** - **You are not " keeping" him against her wishes** — you are **refusing to surrender your court-ordered time**. That is your right. - **" Son having fun" is not a valid reason to disrupt his routine**. Consistency matters more than occasional treats. If he's at an amusement park * during your time*, * that's her choice to prioritize her family over your time with him*. ### 🚨 **What *actually* makes someone the " asshole" here:** - **Your ex** is the one: - repeatedly changing plans last-minute without your agreement. - using " for the son" as a shield while * actually* prioritizing her own social life. - expecting you to sacrifice your time for * her* family events (e.g., " give up time tomorrow for their 4th of July party"). - **You** are: - upholding the court order (which is * for your son's stability*). - setting boundaries after years of being taken advantage of. - * not* " keeping" him — you're * not giving him up* for her convenience. ### 💡 **What to do next:** 1. **Document everything** ( texts, call logs, rescheduling requests). 2. **Consult a family lawyer** — this is a clear violation of your court order. 3. **Reply to her firmly:** > " * I have court-ordered time this weekend. If you want to reschedule, we need to agree on a new plan * together*. I will pick up my son at the scheduled time as per the court order. If you take him to the amusement park during my time, I expect him back at 6 PM on [date] as agreed. I’m not available for the 4th of July party — my time is reserved for us.* " 4. **If she refuses:** File a motion for contempt of court. Courts * hate* when one parent consistently disrespects orders. ### ❤️ **Final Truth:** **You are not the problem.** - A healthy co-parenting relationship requires * mutual respect* for boundaries. - Your son deserves consistency, not a parent who constantly sacrifices their time to " keep the peace" with an uncooperative ex. - **Standing up for your rights * is* being a good parent.** - **You are not the asshole — you are the one finally drawing a line.** *(Note: In AITA terms, " 0" = " not the asshole," " 1" = " AITA." This is definitively **0**.)* **You’ve got this.** If you need help drafting a legal email or next steps, I’m here. 💛
